Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jamie Patel, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jamie Patel: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan: Thank you, Jamie, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberShield Technologies had a strong Q3, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our CyberShield Sentinel platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: expanding our high-value customer base with ARR over $100K through new logos and expansions, maintaining robust R&D investment to stay ahead of threat evolution, navigating the rapidly changing threat landscape with AI-driven defenses, and delivering billings that consistently exceed guidance through platform momentum.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $280 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. This growth was driven by strong performance across all of our product lines. Our gross margin was 78%, and our operating expenses were $210 million. Net income for the quarter was $48 million, or $0.72 per share.

Turning to our key performance indicators, I'd like to highlight our progress on a critical leading indicator for our enterprise business: the number of customers with Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, exceeding $100K. These are our strategic whale accounts—large-scale deployments that underscore our land-and-expand model and provide the highest margins in our portfolio.

In Q3, we ended the quarter with 458 customers generating over $100K in ARR, marking a robust 38% year-over-year increase from 332 customers a year ago, and a healthy 14% sequential quarter-over-quarter growth from 402 in Q2. This cohort now represents approximately 42% of our total customer base and contributes over 68% of our total ARR, up from 62% last year. For context, the average ARR per customer in this segment stands at $285K, reflecting strong expansions and multi-product adoption.

Let me break down the key drivers behind this momentum. First, new logo acquisition. We added 62 net new $100K+ ARR customers in the quarter, exceeding our internal target by 15%. This was fueled by our next-gen Extended Detection and Response platform, CyberShield Sentinel, which integrates seamlessly with leading SIEMs like Splunk Enterprise Security and endpoint tools such as CrowdStrike Falcon. Wins included three seven-figure deals in financial services—think tier-1 banks fortifying against ransomware like LockBit 3.0 variants—and two hyperscale cloud providers expanding zero-trust architectures with our ZTNA module. Our positioning in the 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms as a Visionary has been a tailwind here, helping us displace legacy players like Symantec in regulated verticals.

Second, expansion within the base. Our Net Revenue Retention for this $100K+ cohort hit 128% in Q3, driven by 115 upsell expansions averaging $92K in additional ARR per deal. Customers are layering on our AI-powered Autonomous Threat Hunting capability, which leverages machine learning models trained on 15 trillion daily signals to achieve 99.2% mean time to detect for advanced persistent threats. Healthcare providers, in particular, expanded post our HIPAA-compliant integrations, with 22 accounts adding our Cloud Workload Protection Platform amid rising supply-chain risks echoing the Change Healthcare breach earlier this year.

Vertical and regional insights show financial services now accounting for 35% of this cohort, up 5 points year-over-year, propelled by Dodd-Frank and DORA compliance mandates in Europe. Healthcare grew to 22%, benefiting from our SOC 2 Type II attestation and ransomware indemnity clauses. By region: North America remains dominant at 72% of the total with 329 customers, with EMEA surging 52% year-over-year to 85 customers on GDPR enforcement and NIS2 Directive tailwinds—we're seeing particular strength in the DACH region with wins at two Bundesbank-regulated institutions. APAC, at 8% with 37 customers, is our fastest-growing theater at 67% year-over-year expansion, anchored by partnerships with AWS Tokyo and Singapore hubs, targeting telcos vulnerable to state-sponsored actors like APT41.

Strategically, this $100K+ customer growth validates our platformization shift. In a market where IDC projects global cybersecurity spending to hit $212 billion in 2025—up 14% amid geopolitical tensions and AI-exploited vulnerabilities like those in the Ivanti zero-days—we're outpacing the industry. Our focus on mega-logos over $1M ARR now stands at 47 customers, up 25% year-over-year, with a pipeline of 180 qualified opportunities entering Q4, weighted toward multi-year contracts with 20-25% discounts for bundled Sentinel-XDR and our new Managed Detection and Response service.

Looking forward, we guide to 510-530 $100K+ ARR customers by year-end, implying 22-28% sequential growth, assuming stable macro conditions and no major disruptions from events like the U.S. elections. This positions us for $1.2 billion in total ARR by FYE 2025, with these high-value accounts as the growth engine.

Shifting to another key differentiator, our R&D investment as a percentage of revenue. In the cybersecurity industry, where threats evolve faster than Moore's Law—think AI-orchestrated ransomware like LockBit 4.0 or nation-state APTs leveraging zero-day exploits in supply chains—sustained innovation isn't optional; it's existential. Our R&D spend underscores our commitment to staying ahead of adversaries like Conti successors or state actors from Lazarus Group.

For Q3, we reported R&D expenses of $58 million, representing 20.8% of our record $280 million in revenue—up 120 basis points sequentially from 19.6% in Q2 and 250 basis points year-over-year from 18.3% in Q3 FY2023. This brought our trailing twelve-month R&D intensity to 20.1%, firmly in line with top-tier peers like Palo Alto Networks at around 18-20% and CrowdStrike's 22-24%, but ahead of more hardware-centric players like Fortinet at 15%. Revenue grew 32% year-over-year, driven by 35% expansion in our cloud-native SASE and XDR platforms, yet we prioritized R&D acceleration to fuel this momentum.

Let me break down the trends and drivers. Historically, we've trended upward from 16.5% in FY2022, reflecting a deliberate shift post our acquisition of ThreatX for API security. Q3's uptick was fueled by three pillars: First, AI/ML and Autonomous Security Initiatives, accounting for 45% of Q3 R&D spend at about $26 million. We're doubling down on generative AI for threat hunting, integrated across our Nebula XDR platform. Key projects include our ShieldAI Predictor engine, which uses federated learning to detect polymorphic malware with 98% true positive rate at under 0.1% false positive rate—live in beta with 15 Fortune 500 customers. This addresses the 300% surge in AI-generated phishing per our Q2 Threat Report, mirroring Verizon's DBIR findings. We're also investing $9 million in post-quantum cryptography libraries compliant with NIST's Kyber and Dilithium standards, future-proofing against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

Second, Zero-Trust and Cloud Workload Protection, 30% of spend at around $17.4 million: Enhancements to our ZeroTrust Edge platform, now supporting SASE 2.0 with inline decryption at 100Gbps scales. This counters the 40% year-over-year rise in cloud misconfigurations per our data, competing directly with Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange. We've allocated $5.5 million here for Kubernetes-native runtime security with our proprietary behavioral analytics.

Third, Talent and Ecosystem Investments, 25% of spend at about $14.5 million: Headcount grew 18% quarter-over-quarter to 850 engineers, with key hires from Check Point and Darktrace in Israel and Bangalore. This includes $4.5 million in M&A scouting for SOAR capabilities and partnerships like our expanded integration with AWS Bedrock for sovereign AI in regulated verticals.

Regionally, our R&D intensity varies strategically. In North America, 72% of revenue, it's steady at 19%, focused on hyperscaler integrations amid 25% year-over-year subscription growth. EMEA, 15% of revenue, saw elevated spend at 23% of regional revenue, driven by NIS2 Directive compliance and €10 million in grants for our EU CloudSec Hub in Dublin—addressing the 50% spike in GDPR fines per ENISA reports. APAC, 13% of revenue, hit 25% intensity, with $6.5 million earmarked for China-localized data sovereignty solutions under the PIPL and CSRC rules, plus Japan expansions countering rising ransomware from LockBit affiliates. This regional tilt supports our 45% APAC ARR growth.

Strategically, this investment yields tangible ROI: 28% of Q3 bookings stemmed from R&D-launched features, like ShieldAI's autonomous SOAR, contributing a 3x LTV:CAC uplift. Our patent portfolio swelled to 245, with 40 filed in Q3 on ML anomaly detection. Looking forward, we guide FY2024 R&D at 20-22% of revenue, assuming 25-28% top-line growth to $1.05-1.08 billion, with acceleration in H2 as AI capex matures. This positions us to capture share in the $85 billion TAM per Gartner, outpacing commoditized endpoint players. We're not just spending; we're building an unassailable moat in an industry where 70% of breaches exploit known vulns older than 12 months per our data.

Finally, on billings performance, which came in exceptionally strong at $295 million, representing a 6% beat to the midpoint of our guidance range of $275 million to $280 million. This marks the fourth consecutive quarter of billings outperformance and underscores the accelerating demand for our integrated cybersecurity platform amid a rapidly evolving threat landscape.

On a year-over-year basis, Q3 billings grew 37%, up from 32% in Q2, driven by a combination of new logo wins, expansions with existing customers, and multi-year commitments. Sequentially, billings increased 18% from Q2's $250 million, reflecting seasonal strength in enterprise renewals and the ramp-up of our Sentinel platform's AI-powered modules.

Core drivers behind this outperformance start with our endpoint and cloud workload protection segments. Sentinel Prevent and Sentinel Insight XDR saw 45% year-over-year billings growth, fueled by enterprises hardening their defenses against ransomware-as-a-service campaigns like LockBit 3.0 variants, which spiked 28% in Q3 per our threat intelligence data. We also closed 12 deals over $10 million ACV, including a landmark $25 million multi-year contract with a top-5 global bank for our Sentinel Cloud Security suite—our first hyperscale deployment integrating with AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing workloads.

Customer expansion remains a hallmark, with dollar-based net retention reaching 128% for the quarter, up 200 basis points from Q2. This was propelled by upsells into Sentinel Exposure Management, where we saw 55% year-over-year growth as customers prioritized attack surface management post high-profile breaches like the Change Healthcare incident earlier this year. Our AI-native Next-Gen SIEM, Sentinel LogScale, contributed $120 million in incremental billings, a 60% year-over-year jump, as we displaced legacy solutions from Splunk and Elastic in 40% of those deals.

Regionally, performance was balanced but with notable bright spots. The Americas drove 65% of total billings at 42% year-over-year growth, anchored by Fortune 500 wins in financial services and healthcare—sectors grappling with HIPAA and PCI-DSS compliance pressures amid rising phishing volumes up 35% month-over-month. EMEA delivered $192 million, or 28% year-over-year growth, tempered slightly by macroeconomic headwinds in Germany and the UK, but boosted by GDPR-driven mandates and our new Paris data residency zone, which secured three sovereign cloud deals with EU public sector entities. APAC was the fastest grower at 52% year-over-year to $145 million, led by Japan and Australia, where our partnership with NTT Docomo for Sentinel Zero Trust has resonated amid surging state-sponsored APT activity from Lazarus Group affiliates.

Strategically, this billings beat positions us exceptionally well for FY'25. Our total RPO now stands at $4.2 billion, up 42% year-over-year, with current RPO at $2.8 billion growing 38%. This gives us high confidence in our FY'25 billings guidance of $3.55 billion to $3.60 billion, implying 30%+ growth at the midpoint. Key initiatives include deeper integration with Microsoft Azure Sentinel via our Sentinel Fusion orchestration layer, targeting $500 million in co-sell pipeline, and the Q4 launch of Sentinel Air Gap for air-gapped OT environments, addressing ICS/OT cyber risks highlighted in the recent CISA alerts on Volt Typhoon infrastructure attacks.

In summary, our billings outperformance validates the flywheel effect of our platformization strategy in a market where IDC projects cybersecurity spending to hit $212 billion globally in 2025, up 14%. We're not just riding the wave of macro threats—we're leading it with purpose-built, AI-accelerated innovations.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: [Instructions for Q&A session]. Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your touchtone phone. We'll pause for a moment to assemble our roster. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs.

Alex Rivera: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter, team. I wanted to dive into your commentary on the evolving threat landscape. With ransomware payouts hitting record highs and AI weaponization accelerating, how are you seeing this play out across your customer base, and what does it mean for your go-forward initiatives?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Alex, and thanks for the kind words on Q3. Let me unpack the threat landscape as we've observed it firsthand across our 4,200 enterprise customers, including 28% of the Fortune 100. The environment is more dynamic and pernicious than ever, with cybercrime evolving from opportunistic hacks to sophisticated, state-sponsored operations. I'll break this down by key vectors, trends, regional nuances, and our strategic positioning.

First, ransomware remains the apex predator. We've seen a 142% year-over-year increase in ransomware incidents reported through our Managed Detection and Response service, aligning with Chainalysis data showing global extortion payments surpassing $1.1 billion in 2023—up from $450 million just two years prior. What's new is the double and triple extortion playbook: attackers not only encrypt data but exfiltrate it for public shaming or auction on dark web forums like LockBit's successor sites. Our telemetry shows an average dwell time of 11 days for these attacks, down from 21 days last year due to better EDR adoption, but the mean recovery cost has ballooned to $4.7 million per incident, per our anonymized customer data.

Shifting to AI-driven threats, this is the accelerant pouring on the fire. Adversaries are leveraging generative AI for hyper-personalized phishing—think deepfake voice clones in vishing attacks, which spiked 320% in our global SOC feeds. We've blocked over 2.7 million such attempts in Q3 alone via our AI-powered Behavioral Analytics Engine, which uses unsupervised ML to detect anomalies 40% faster than legacy SIEMs like Splunk or Elastic. Nation-state actors, tracked via MITRE ATT&CK TTPs like T1566 Phishing, are now automating lateral movement with tools mimicking legitimate LLMs, evading traditional signature-based defenses.

Supply chain compromises are another red-hot vector, echoing SolarWinds and the recent MOVEit breach. We've observed a 95% year-over-year uptick in third-party risks, with 62% of incidents originating from vendor ecosystems. Our Supply Chain Risk Management module, integrated with our XDR platform, has identified 15,000+ vulnerabilities in customer software bills of materials this quarter, prioritizing those with CVSS scores above 8.0.

On the cloud front, misconfigurations account for 37% of breaches in our dataset, up from 28% in 2022, driven by multi-cloud sprawl—AWS, Azure, and GCP each representing 25-30% of exposures. Zero-trust adoption is our counter: 72% of our new logos in Q3 opted for our SASE-plus solution, which enforces micro-segmentation and continuous authentication, reducing blast radius by 85% in simulated red-team exercises.

Regionally, the picture varies sharply. In North America, which drives 52% of our ARR, threats are enterprise-focused, with 40% tied to IP theft—think Chinese APT41 groups targeting manufacturing. EMEA, 28% of ARR, sees GDPR-fueled compliance attacks, like the 25% rise in DPO-targeted spear-phishing amid new NIS2 regs. APAC, 15% ARR, is the growth hotspot but also the hotspot for chaos: geopolitical tensions have fueled a 210% surge in destructive wipers from North Korean Lazarus actors, hitting financials in Japan and South Korea. LatAm rounds out at 5%, where crypto-jacking via Magecart-style skimmers jumped 180%.

Strategically, we're leaning in with three pillars: Proactive AI Defenses, with $150 million invested in our NeoGen platform, which fuses GenAI with federated learning across customer endpoints—yielding 97% true positive rates on novel threats, benchmarked against CrowdStrike's Falcon and Palo Alto's Cortex XDR. Quantum-Resistant Roadmap: With harvest-now-decrypt-later risks from Shor's algorithm looming, we're rolling out post-quantum cryptography hybrids like Kyber and Dilithium in our VPN and email gateways, ahead of NIST's 2024 standardization. Ecosystem Alliances: Deep integrations with Okta for identity, ServiceNow for orchestration, and our new JV with Zscaler for converged SASE/SSO, capturing 35% market share in the $85 billion SASE TAM per Gartner.

Bottom line, Alex: threats are industrializing—volume up 28% quarter-over-quarter, sophistication via AI up 4x—but so are our defenses. This landscape drove our 32% ARR growth and 150 basis points margin expansion, positioning us for $2.1 billion in FY24 revenue. We're not just reacting; we're architecting resilience.

Operator: Next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley.

Maria Lopez: Congrats on the beat. Can you expand on how your R&D investments are translating to product adoption?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Maria. Our R&D focus on AI/ML, zero-trust, and talent is directly fueling adoption, as Lisa detailed earlier. For instance, ShieldAI Predictor is already in beta with Fortune 500s, driving upsells.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Singh with JPMorgan.

Raj Singh: Great results. Thoughts on go-to-market for APAC expansions?

David Harlan: Thanks, Raj. APAC is accelerating with 67% growth in our $100K+ cohort there, anchored by AWS partnerships and tailored solutions for state-sponsored threats like APT41.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays.

Emily Carter: Solid quarter. Any updates on RPO trends versus billings?

Lisa Chen: Emily, our RPO is up 42% to $4.2 billion, supporting the billings guidance we laid out—high confidence in 30%+ FY'25 growth.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

David Harlan: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Jamie Patel: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
